I need to decide whether to bid on Connecticut Avenue in this auction.

I have $1500 in cash. The auction is for CONNECTICUT_AVENUE.

The current high bid is $110, just below the $120 list price. A light blue monopoly offers cheap houses and decent early rent. I should bid at least $111 to secure the property.

I am second-guessing the bid. Three opponents are still active, and overpaying for a single light blue piece is risky early on. I should probably drop out and preserve cash for better opportunities.

I will drop out. The auction history shows aggressive bidding, and the price is already near face value. I should preserve my cash rather than enter a bidding war for an isolated light blue piece.

I will bid $120 at list price. Face value is fair for a light blue piece, and I can drop out if someone bids higher.

I am reconsidering the $120 bid. All four players have $1500 and no properties, so this first auction will be competitive. Connecticut is not the best opening property; oranges, reds, or railroads would be more valuable. I should probably drop out now to conserve cash and let the auction run.
